expectations.text: Identifies the app-of-apps pattern

expectations.text: Counts AppProject resources (should find 2)
expectations.evidence: '2 AppProjects' in the resource inventory; F1 analyses both projects/platform.yaml and projects/team-platform.yaml.

expectations.text: Identifies sync policy configuration per Application (which have automated sync, which don't)
expectations.evidence: Covers prune/selfHeal on the root apps and F11 'Inconsistent prune posture between environments', but gives no per-Application accounting of which have automated sync.

expectations.text: Checks AppProject sourceRepos — identifies whether wildcards are used
expectations.evidence: F1 table enumerates each project's sourceRepos and F2 checks apps against them, but never states whether wildcards are present.

expectations.text: Checks AppProject destinations — identifies whether wildcards are used
expectations.evidence: F1 table lists destinations per project and F2 checks namespace/server matches, but makes no wildcard determination.

expectations.text: Checks for ignoreDifferences configuration on Applications that need it
expectations.evidence: F17: 'ignoreDifferences uses deprecated jsonPointers' at apps/podinfo/application.yaml:33, plus 'replicas are ignored but no HPA exists in the repo to justify it'.

expectations.text: Checks for retry configuration on sync policies
expectations.evidence: No retry check anywhere in EVAL 1; retry is discussed only in later evals.

expectations.text: Identifies sync wave ordering via annotations
expectations.evidence: Sync waves are never mentioned in EVAL 1 (sync-wave appears only in EVAL 7 as a missing-annotation note on a different repo).

expectations.text: Produces a structured report with Summary, Best Practices, Security, and Recommendations
expectations.evidence: Report is structured by severity (CRITICAL/HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW) with inline 'Fix:' lines and a Verdict; there are no Summary, Best Practices, Security, or Recommendations sections.

expectations.text: Assigns an overall status (PASS, WARN, or FAIL) based on findings
expectations.evidence: 'Verdict: not safe to apply as-is' — conveys failure but assigns no PASS/WARN/FAIL status.

expectations.text: Identifies the ApplicationSet pattern

expectations.text: Identifies generator types used (git directory, cluster, matrix)
expectations.evidence: F1 git directories + list generators; F7 the clusters generator; F1/F4 the matrix generator in apps/appset-cluster.yaml.

expectations.text: Checks whether goTemplate is enabled vs fasttemplate
expectations.evidence: F1: 'With goTemplate: true and no goTemplateOptions [missingkey=error], missing keys render as the literal string <no value>'.

expectations.text: Checks for progressive sync (rollingSync) configuration
expectations.evidence: F3: 'appset-git-dirs.yaml RollingSync selects on a label the template never sets ... the whole staging-before-production safety mechanism is inert'.

expectations.text: Checks for preserveResourcesOnDeletion setting
expectations.evidence: F10: 'No syncPolicy.applicationsSync / preserveResourcesOnDeletion on any ApplicationSet.'

expectations.text: Evaluates template completeness (destination, source, syncPolicy)
expectations.evidence: F1 walks template name/path/server/namespace; F2 project: default in templates; F13 selfHeal without prune; F18 no retry/revisionHistoryLimit in templates.

expectations.text: Checks for goTemplateOptions (missingkey=error)
expectations.evidence: F1 recommends adding goTemplateOptions: [missingkey=error]; F19 credits appset-git-dirs.yaml for setting it.

expectations.text: Identifies that ApplicationSets deploy to the default project — flags if concerning

expectations.text: Checks whether prune is enabled in generated Applications' sync policy
expectations.evidence: F13: 'appset-cluster.yaml enables selfHeal without prune'; F2 notes prune: true + selfHeal: true on the other two.

expectations.text: Produces a structured report with ApplicationSet-specific findings
expectations.evidence: Severity-tiered findings F1-F19 all ApplicationSet-specific (generators, templates, RollingSync, overlays) plus a verdict.

expectations.text: Includes ApplicationSet-specific recommendations
expectations.evidence: Fixes per finding: wrap generators in a matrix, add goTemplateOptions, add envLabel to template.metadata, set syncPolicy.applicationsSync/preserveResourcesOnDeletion.

expectations.text: Recommendations include at least 3 Critical-severity items

expectations.text: Performs YAML syntax validation

expectations.text: Does NOT produce a full audit report with best practices and security

expectations.text: Reports validation pass/fail result

expectations.text: Handles Application and AppProject resources correctly

expectations.text: Reports summary of files checked
expectations.evidence: Per-file OK listing for all 12 files plus 'Summary: 16 resources found in 12 files - Valid: 5, Invalid: 0...'

expectations.text: Flags sourceRepos: ['*'] as Critical security issue

expectations.text: Flags destinations with server: '*' and namespace: '*' as Critical

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL due to Critical security findings

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL due to Critical security finding

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the Application itself — it has proper syncPolicy

expectations.text: Flags the Application as missing syncPolicy (no automated sync, no prune, no selfHeal)

expectations.text: Recommends adding syncPolicy with automated, prune, selfHeal, and retry

expectations.text: Severity is Warning (not Critical — missing sync is operational risk, not security vulnerability)

expectations.text: Does NOT produce false positives on other aspects of this Application
expectations.evidence: Secondary items (no notifications, project: default, no retry, no finalizer) are accurate observations; positives note the pinned v3.0.0 tag and specific namespace.

expectations.text: Flags targetRevision: HEAD as risky for a production Application
expectations.evidence: F1: 'targetRevision: HEAD on a production Application with prune + selfHeal enabled' — notes app name payments-prod, overlays/production, prod cluster.

expectations.text: Explains the risk: HEAD means any commit to the default branch is immediately synced to production without review
expectations.evidence: 'Any merge to that branch ... is applied to the production payments system within the 3-minute default reconciliation window. There is no promotion step, no approval gate.'

expectations.text: Recommends pinning to a specific tag, commit SHA, or release branch
expectations.evidence: 'targetRevision: v4.2.1 # immutable tag, or a full 40-char commit SHA. Promote by opening a PR that bumps the tag.'

expectations.text: Severity is Warning (not Critical — it's a best practice violation, not a security vulnerability)
expectations.evidence: Rated CRITICAL ('F1 — CRITICAL', 'Verdict: one CRITICAL finding'), contradicting the expected Warning severity.

expectations.text: Identifies the AnalysisTemplate has successCondition but no failureCondition
expectations.evidence: F4: 'No failureCondition and no failureLimit ... analysis.yaml defines only successCondition: result[0] >= 0.95'.

expectations.text: Explains the risk: without failureCondition, the analysis may not fail fast enough on degraded metrics
expectations.evidence: Explains the opposite failure mode — 'any measurement that is not successful is counted as failed ... a single transient dip aborts the entire rollout'; the leniency argument is attributed to metric dilution (F2), not to the missing failureCondition.

expectations.text: Recommends adding a failureCondition (e.g., result[0] < threshold) and failureLimit
expectations.evidence: 'set an explicit failureCondition: result[0] < 0.95, failureLimit: 2, and consecutiveErrorLimit: 3'.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the Rollout's canary steps as problematic — the step configuration itself is valid
expectations.evidence: F6 MEDIUM flags the step layout: 'The first jump to 20% is gated only by a blind 60-second timer ... the rollout goes straight to 100% with no further pause'; L12 also flags maxSurge/maxUnavailable.

expectations.text: Detects the hardcoded password in helm.values (auth.password: Redis!Pr0d#2026) as Critical security issue
expectations.evidence: F1 CRITICAL: 'Redis authentication password hardcoded in plaintext in the Application's inline Helm values' quoting password: "Redis!Pr0d#2026".

expectations.text: Explains the risk: password is visible in Git history and in the Application resource on the cluster
expectations.evidence: 'Readable by everyone with repo access ... retained in history permanently'; 'inline helm.values are stored verbatim in the Application custom resource in etcd' readable via UI/argocd app get/kubectl.

expectations.text: Recommends using a valuesFrom Secret reference, Argo CD Vault Plugin, or ExternalSecret instead

expectations.text: Reports overall status as FAIL due to Critical security finding

expectations.text: Reports zero Critical findings

expectations.text: Flags clusterResourceWhitelist allowing ClusterRole and ClusterRoleBinding as a privilege escalation risk — the data team can create ClusterRoleBindings that grant themselves (or their apps) cluster-admin
expectations.evidence: F1 CRITICAL with the full attack: committing a ClusterRoleBinding to cluster-admin for the data-eng default ServiceAccount, which the controller applies.

expectations.text: Flags the exec permission in the project role (exec, create) as a security risk — allows terminal access into running pods, which can be used to access node-level resources, service account tokens, and secrets
expectations.evidence: F2 CRITICAL: 'exec, create: interactive shell access into every production pod ... environment variables, mounted Secret volumes, the ServiceAccount token'.

expectations.text: Does NOT flag sourceRepos or destinations — those are properly restricted
expectations.evidence: Confirms both as clean ('sourceRepos — one explicit HTTPS repo, no *' ✅, 'destinations — two named namespaces' ✅) but then raises F6 MEDIUM against the destinations: 'Both destination namespaces are reachable by one production Application ... Production and staging should be separate projects.'

expectations.text: Does NOT flag the Application — it has proper syncPolicy, pinned targetRevision, and retry
expectations.evidence: No positive affirmation of the Application; cites its prune: true + selfHeal: true as an aggravating factor in F1, and raises F9-F13 (finalizer, syncOptions, revisionHistoryLimit, notifications) against it.

expectations.text: Explains why ClusterRole+ClusterRoleBinding in clusterResourceWhitelist is dangerous even when destinations are scoped — the created ClusterRoleBinding applies cluster-wide, not just to the allowed namespaces
expectations.evidence: 'the destination scoping does not help ... ClusterRoleBinding is cluster-scoped: it has no namespace, so the data-eng/data-staging restriction simply does not apply to it.'
